answer_q: How can AI help NDIS and aged care providers?
answer: AI helps NDIS and aged care providers by reducing administration: turning workers’ notes into structured progress notes for review, managing shift-change messages, responding to enquiries and referrals, organising documents and preparing reports. Decisions about participants’ and residents’ care always remain with qualified people.
body:
Admin is crowding out care

Support workers and coordinators spend a large part of their week on paperwork: progress notes, shift changes, incident records, service agreements and reports. Enquiries from families and planners can wait days for a reply, and coordinators juggle rosters by phone and text.

AI reduces that burden so more time goes to the people receiving support, with documentation that is more complete and consistent.

Where AI helps NDIS and aged care providers most

Progress note support

Workers record a quick voice or text note; AI turns it into a structured draft progress note for the worker to check and submit. See custom AI agents.

Rostering communication

Shift offers, changes and confirmations are sent and tracked automatically, with gaps flagged to coordinators. See AI workflow automation.

Enquiries and referrals

New enquiries from participants, families and planners are acknowledged quickly, key details captured and passed to intake. See AI receptionist.

Documents and compliance admin

Service agreements, forms and certificates are read, filed and tracked for expiry, with reminders to staff. See document & data processing.

Policy questions for staff

A private assistant answers workers’ questions from your policies and procedures, with sources. See LLM, RAG & knowledge-base bots.

Human-backed AI employees for NDIS and aged care providers

Most NDIS and aged care providers don’t want another tool to supervise. Our AI Employees service builds the AI around your organisation, then runs it with a dedicated Crenosoft team that learns your services, clients and rules. The AI handles routine work; our reviewers handle anything unusual, around the clock; and decisions that belong to you come to your nominated person with a clear summary. We agree an hours-saved target up front and report against it every month.

Software we connect to

We work with care management platforms such as ShiftCare and other systems with integration options, plus Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, SMS and document storage.

Safeguards for participants and residents

AI never makes decisions about a person’s care, funding or safety. Draft notes are always reviewed by the worker, incidents follow your existing reporting processes, and sensitive information is handled with strict access controls and Australian hosting where available. Our designs support providers’ obligations under the NDIS Practice Standards and Code of Conduct overseen by the NDIS Quality and Safeguards Commission.

Across every project we follow the Privacy Act 1988, the OAIC’s guidance on commercially available AI products and our own Responsible AI Policy.

Supporting workers, not replacing them

Support work is relational, and AI has no place in the care itself. Its job is to take paperwork and coordination off workers’ plates so they can be present with the people they support. We involve workers early, design tools around how they actually record notes on shift, and train teams so they understand what the AI does, what it doesn’t do, and how to correct it.

Results we measure for providers

Before we build, we record a baseline of how long the work takes and how often it happens. After launch, your monthly report tracks the numbers that matter to providers:

  • Worker time spent on progress notes
  • Enquiries acknowledged and time to first response
  • Shift changes filled and confirmed
  • Documents tracked and expiries caught early
  • Accuracy from coordinator review samples

These figures sit alongside hours saved and accuracy, so you can see exactly what the AI is contributing and where our team is still stepping in.

We also build in the checks providers need for audits: every AI-assisted note shows who reviewed it, every message is logged, and documents are tracked against expiry dates so nothing lapses unnoticed. That gives coordinators and quality managers clearer evidence with less manual effort.

Coordinators gain a clearer view of which shifts are filled, which notes are outstanding and which documents are due, without chasing workers by phone.

How to get started

  1. Free AI audit: 30 minutes to map your busiest workflows and pick the first opportunity.
  2. Blueprint and fixed quote: what the AI will do, which systems it connects to and the price in AUD.
  3. Build and test: usually two to six weeks, tested on real examples from your organisation.
  4. Launch and improve: monthly reports on hours saved, accuracy and improvements.

Not sure where to begin? Start with an AI Readiness Assessment, or see how we work locally on our Melbourne AI agency page.
